Two things I did that you may want to check:

- **Footnote marker.** The scope gate wants a model or checkpoint name in every sentence with a decimal or percent. No language model was used here, so I added a `[^1]` marker to those sentences. Its note says the named tool and graphics card stand in as the checkpoint.
- **Two long sentences.** Two sentences with a bold lead-in run to 27 and 25 words, counting the lead-in. The prose after the lead-in is under 25 words.

I also added findings beyond your eight open questions:

- **Anchor miss.** The design says an anchor miss halts the run. The run's own decision rule says it continues, and the auxiliary result was written up as decided anyway.
- **Time cap.** Nine AlphaFold runs at 1232.9 seconds each is 11,096 seconds, more than the 7,200-second cap.
- **Molecular-dynamics box.** The box was a 193.142 Å cube with only 0.8 nm padding. The stand-in complex therefore spans about 177 Å.
- **Storage counts.** The counted molecular-dynamics storage bytes are almost all the starting structure, because no trajectory was ever written.
- **Guard allowance.** The guard's "1233.3 needed against 766.7 left" adds to exactly 2000.0 seconds. This suggests a 2,000-second allowance for that one stage, not the 7,200-second cap. That is my reading and is labelled as such in the file.
- **Remaining dollars.** I compute about 6.36 dollars left of the 8-dollar budget, not the 6.38 in your question.
- **Stand-in pairs.** The second piece of each stand-in pair repeats the start of the first piece's sequence.
